description:
Goal (separate arc)
Lift the SemanticClosed barrier so DeriveExecutableTransport(E) fires pre-closure, co-settling transport with activations inside the one fixpoint loop. Full realization of the northstar invariant through the backend seam.

What
- Drop the SemanticClosed gate on DeriveExecutableTransport; gate each prerequisite on Current/Settled facts the way derive_runtime_demand waits on current, not settled (jobs/runtime_demand.rs:237-244).
- No new data model: the Stage-2 agreement cell and InputShape contributions already converge on ASCENDING contributors by quiescence, exactly like ActivationInputs (jobs/semantic.rs:205-206). The caller set need not be known up front; it accumulates.
- Retire the seal runtime_demands re-gather seam (jobs/root.rs:302-318) and closure.runtime_demands consumption if nothing else needs the blob.
- Confirm and delete now-dead Cycle/Tarjan and ProjectionMemo if any remnants survive earlier stages.

Risk
Caller-set narrowing: a late caller contribution dropped on a rebased rerun. Guard with the contribution withdrawal-on-rebase semantics (semantic.rs:746-780) and the equivalence harness driven WITHOUT forcing closure first.

Verify
shadow==monolith green; transport facts observed settling before SemanticClosed in telemetry; full matrix + lib green; zero warnings.

comments.text: Deferred as the explicitly-separate Stage-4 arc (the ticket's own 'Goal (separate arc)' label). Confirmed against code: both derive_executable_transport AND the derive_transport_plan fan-in read world.semantic_closure (the executable SET + runtime_demands), which only exists after the seal (SemanticClosed). collect_transport_contexts iterates closure.executables. So lifting the barrier requires the executable set + per-executable contexts to be readable incrementally (contexts-as-facts / co-settling) -- a substantial data-model change. Marginal current benefit: batch compilation (fz2 build / the test matrix) settles the closure once regardless, so co-settling only pays off for incremental recompilation, which isn't exercised today. Core arc (5.1/5.3/5.4) complete and green; 5.5 is the value-when-incrementality-matters follow-on.

Re-opened for completion. Step 1 (pull->push inversion) landed as fz-xhk (9ad642c69): the two backward whole-closure scans in the per-exec projection (collect_call_arg_input_sources, collect_callable_capture_input_sources) are now a forward index built once when contexts assemble, bundled as TransportContexts. Byte-identical (transport 72/0, shadow green, 13 pre-existing lib reds unchanged), deterministic, perf-positive. Remaining DAG: (2) promote the forward index to an ascending contributed fact InputSources(E) [ContributionMap]; (3) bounded callee/producer context lookups -> per-exec fact reads; (4) drop SemanticClosed gate on DeriveExecutableTransport(E); (5) retire seal runtime_demands re-gather + closure.runtime_demands consumers. Fan-in DeriveTransportPlan stays gated (whole-root artifact). Pre-existing flaky test fz-0lm surfaced + filed.

Steps 1+2 landed (fz-xhk 9ad642c69, fz-mmh e4c1ea22e), both byte-identical + verified. The per-exec transport job's INPUT data now flows through the ascending InputSources contributed fact, not a backward closure scan -- the genuine forward-propagation inversion. GATE-DROP code-confirmed blocked on two deeper rewrites: (1) project_one_executable transitively reaches callee/producer CONTEXTS via the prebuilt whole-closure map; bounded neighborhood diverges (missing context -> SourceShape::Unknown), so pre-seal projection needs a demand-driven rewrite (project_source + ~15 helpers WAIT on a missing neighbor's per-exec facts instead of a prebuilt map); (2) world.semantic_closure is published atomically by SealSemanticClosure (no partial closure pre-seal), so firing pre-closure needs the executable SET published incrementally -- a SealSemanticClosure rewrite beyond transport. Neither alone drops the gate. Payoff (co-settling) unverifiable here (fz-g2f not built; native red).

INVESTIGATION (this session, code-proven; WIP in git stash, NOT committed -- sprawl). The blocker I recorded earlier was a MISDIAGNOSIS: the executable SET is already incremental (Executable(E)/RuntimeDemand(E) facts published per-exec by seed_root/analyze_activation); no SealSemanticClosure rewrite is needed. derive_runtime_demand is the working template for the per-exec shape.

THREE things were proven:
1. SIGNAL BUILT (fz-g2f): in-process test drives a root to settle, adds a 2nd defimpl on a value-joined Shout.say call (ProtocolDispatch bump grows the closure), asserts an unrelated executable (lonely, reached only via zero-arg quiet -> cone {lonely,quiet}, disjoint from the perturbed shouty/main) is NOT re-projected. RED at HEAD (SemanticClosed rebases ALL transport readers). Telemetry instrument added: executable_transport.derived event (per (re)projection) in define_executable_transport.
2. PRECISE CONE WORKS: rewrote the per-exec job to gather contexts for EXACTLY project_one_executable(E)'s transitive access set (build_executable_context per-exec from facts; recording-narrow proves gathered==accessed). With this, g2f goes GREEN and the shadow==monolith + 72/0 transport contract tests stay BYTE-IDENTICAL. A naive worklist OVER-approximates (blanket producer/callee expansion pulls quiet->main->shouty, re-coupling lonely to the perturbed shouty) -- the cone MUST be value-source-directed.
3. TRUE GATE-DROP BLOCKER (precisely isolated): firing transport pre-seal hits project_callable_value's assert -- RuntimeDemand(E).callable_flows is empty pre-seal while demand.is_callable(). Naive Unknown-and-publish yields WRONG shapes (cascade ~24 reds). Literal co-settling needs projection to DEFER (don't publish; wait on the unascended fact; re-run as it ascends) -- a real redesign of project_one_executable's control flow, broader than one site.

REFRAME (decision needed): fz-g2f says the VALUE is bounded blast radius, not literally 'transport before seal'. That value is achievable POST-seal by subscribing transport(E) to its PRECISE CONE only (not the global SemanticClosed): transport(E) is a pure function of its cone, so NOT re-running it when an unrelated impl is added is correct-by-construction, not stale. This sidesteps the pre-seal projection-correctness problem entirely. Recommend redefining 5.5 around 'cone-scoped subscription' rather than 'pre-seal firing', implemented as ONE clean focused change from HEAD (not accreted agents).

ALSO (unverified, agent-reported): a pre-existing demand/analysis fixpoint runaway (~1.8k AnalyzeActivation/DeriveRuntimeDemand re-derivations on heavy enum fixtures, on the committed baseline) -- likely fz-downstream-monolith/fz-8b0 territory; needs its own ticket after independent confirmation.

DONE (e9c320d10) via the cone-scoped-subscription reframe (authorized this session). The literal 'transport settles before SemanticClosed' was found UNNECESSARY for the ticket's value and NOT pursued: it requires a defer-and-not-publish redesign of project_one_executable (multiple sites assert a sealed world; firing pre-seal panics on un-ascended callable_flows, and naive Unknown-and-publish yields wrong shapes). The VALUE (fz-g2f bounded blast radius) is delivered correct-by-construction by subscribing transport(E) to ONLY its precise dependency cone (recording-pass narrowing, byte-identical) and NOT to the global SemanticClosed (polled as a run-gate, not subscribed). transport(E) is a pure function of its cone, so an unrelated change does not rebase it. Verify: fz-g2f GREEN, shadow==monolith green, transport 72/0 deterministic, full lib at its 13 pre-existing native/type-infer reds, clippy -D clean. NOTE: the literal barrier-lift remains theoretically open but is not needed for incremental blast radius; if ever pursued it is the project_one_executable co-settling redesign.

title: Stage 4 (arc): lift the SemanticClosed barrier; co-settle transport in the loop
